'''Jean-Michel Coron''' (born August 8, 1956) is a [[French people|French]] [[mathematician]]. He first studied at [[École Polytechnique]], where he worked on his PhD thesis advised by [[Haïm Brezis]]. Since 1992, he has studied the [[control theory]] of [[partial differential equation]]s, and which includes both control and stabilization.<ref>{{cite book |title=Control and Nonlinearity |url=https://archive.org/details/ost-engineering-coron-book |first=Jean-Michel |last=Coron |publisher=AMS |year=2007 |edition=Hardcover |isbn=978-0-8218-3668-2 }}</ref><ref>See also his [[Scholarpedia]] article: {{cite journal |title=Control of Partial Differential Equations |journal=Scholarpedia |date=2009 |volume=4 |issue=11 |last1=Coron |first1=Jean-Michel |page=6451 |doi=10.4249/scholarpedia.6451 |doi-access=free |bibcode=2009SchpJ...4.6451C }}</ref> His results concern partial differential equations related  to [[fluid dynamics]], with emphasis on nonlinear phenomena, and part of them found applications to control channels.

He had previously worked in the field of non-linear functional analysis,  where he also obtained significant results. Jean-Michel Coron was awarded numerous prizes, such as the [[Fermat Prize|Fermat prize]] in 1993, the [[Peccot Lectures|Peccot lecture]] in 1987, the Jaffé prize in 1995 by the [[French Academy of Sciences|Académie des Sciences]], and the Dargelos prize in 2002.

He was invited at the 1990 [[International Congress of Mathematicians]] (Kyoto)  in the section Partial Differential Equations, and he was also invited as a plenary speaker at  the 2010 International Congress of Mathematicians, Hyderabad, India.<ref>[http://www.icm2010.org.in/ ''International Congress of Mathematicians 2010''] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100208184251/http://www.icm2010.org.in/ |date=2010-02-08 }}</ref> He is an emeritus Professor at [[Sorbonne University]] in Paris, and was a Senior member of the  Institut Universitaire de France between 2003 and 2013.<ref>[http://iuf.amue.fr/author/jcoron/ ''Jean-Michel Coron at IUF''] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081126040535/http://iuf.amue.fr/author/jcoron/ |date=2008-11-26 }}</ref> He is also a member of the Académie des Sciences<ref>[https://www.academie-sciences.fr/pdf/communique/election_191114.pdf ''Election of Jean-Michel Coron at Académie des Sciences''] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250324215441/https://www.academie-sciences.fr/pdf/communique/election_191114.pdf }}</ref> and the [[Academia Europaea]].<ref>[https://www.ae-info.org/ae/Member/Coron_Jean-Michel ''Jean-Michel Coron at Academia Europaea''] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250324215807/https://www.ae-info.org/ae/Member/Coron_Jean-Michel}}</ref>

Jean-Michel Coron is the husband of [[Claire Voisin]] who was also plenary speaker at the 2010 International Congress of Mathematicians and who is the 2016 recipient of the [[CNRS Gold medal|Gold medal]] of the [[French National Centre for Scientific Research]], the highest scientific research award in France.<ref>{{citation|url=http://www2.cnrs.fr/presse/communique/4701.htm|title=La médaille d'or 2016 du CNRS est attribuée à Claire Voisin, mathématicienne|publisher=French National Centre for Scientific Research (CNRS)|date=September 21, 2016|accessdate=2016-10-03}}.</ref> They have five children.<ref>[http://webusers.imj-prg.fr/~claire.voisin/Articlesweb/noticevoisin.pdf ''Curriculum Vitae'']</ref>
